title: Completion-unit normalization of scalar adjunction and pullback reconstruction
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $I$ a finitely generated ideal, $A/I$ additive torsion, and $P_n=A/I^n$ finite and perfect over $A$ for every $n\geq1$. For a scheme $T$, use its small pro-etale site, the constant ring sheaves $\underline A_T$, $\underline{P_n}_T$, and $A_T=\varprojlim_n\underline{P_n}_T$, with canonical scalar map $\underline A_T\to A_T$ and quotient projections [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. All sites are small in [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $D(A_T)$ and $D(\underline A_T)$ for unbounded derived module categories and $r_T$ for restriction along this scalar map [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Let $J=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op}$, $\Delta$ be its constant-diagram functor, and $Q_T=(\underline{P_n}_T)_n$ with quotient transitions. On the ringed diagram site [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization], define $\mathcal R_T^aL=\Delta L\otimes^L_{\Delta A_T}Q_T$ and $\mathcal R_T^0L_0=\Delta L_0\otimes^L_{\Delta\underline A_T}Q_T$. These are actual derived strict towers. For an edge $u:U\to V$ use the canonical coefficient isomorphisms $u^{-1}A_V\cong A_U$, $u^{-1}\underline{P_n}_V\cong\underline{P_n}_U$ [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image], the ordinary ringed operations $L_u^a\dashv R_u^a$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], their strict-diagram operations $\mathscr L_u^a\dashv\mathscr R_u^a$, and the constant-coefficient counterparts $G_u\dashv R_u^0$ and $G_u\dashv R_u^{\mathcal T}$. Let $a_u:r_UL_u^a\cong G_ur_V$, $\chi_u:r_VR_u^a\cong R_u^0r_U$, $p_u:r_U\mathscr L_u^a\cong G_ur_V$ and $d_u:r_V\mathscr R_u^a\cong R_u^{\mathcal T}r_U$ be the normalized flat scalar comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ringed-diagram-restriction].

Put $\mathcal L_T^a=R\lim$ on completed-coefficient strict towers and $\mathcal L_T^0=R\lim$ on constant-coefficient strict towers. Let $\lambda_Z:r_T\mathcal L_T^aZ\cong\mathcal L_T^0r_TZ$ be the compatible-family/K-injective comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-scalar-tower-limit-square], and let $\rho_L$ and $q_{u,L}=(G_u\rho_L)p_{u,\mathcal R_V^aL}$ be the strict balancing and pullback comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-quotient-scalar-balancing]. Derived completeness means invertibility of the canonical quotient completion unit; its equivalence with Koszul completeness is fixed by [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction]. Restriction identifies the two full complete categories [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. Define $F_u^a$ as ordinary pullback followed by quotient completion [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], and $F_u^0=(\mathcal L_U^0\mathcal R_U^0)G_u$ on constant complete inputs [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction]. Denote their completion units from ordinary pullback by $j^a_{u,L}:L_u^aL\to F_u^aL$ and $j^0_{u,r_VL}:G_ur_VL\to F_u^0r_VL$, and their fixed quotient reconstruction isomorphisms by
$$r_{u,L}:F_u^aL\cong\mathcal L_U^a\mathscr L_u^a\mathcal R_V^aL,\quad r^0_{u,r_VL}:F_u^0r_VL\cong\mathcal L_U^0G_u\mathcal R_V^0r_VL.$$

There is a unique natural isomorphism $\phi_u:r_UF_u^a\cong F_u^0r_V$ on the full complete category satisfying $\phi_{u,L}r_U(j^a_{u,L})=j^0_{u,r_VL}a_{u,L}$. Its normalization is
$$\mathcal L_U^0(q_{u,L})\lambda_{\mathscr L_u^a\mathcal R_V^aL}\,r_U(r_{u,L})=r^0_{u,r_VL}\phi_{u,L}.$$
Moreover restriction identifies the actual quotient completion units: under $\lambda$ and $\rho$, $r_T(L\to\mathcal L_T^a\mathcal R_T^aL)$ equals the constant quotient completion unit of $r_TL$, for every ambient $L$.

The comparison $\phi_u$, together with $\chi_u$, identifies the adjunctions $F_u^a\dashv R_u^a$ and $F_u^0\dashv R_u^0$: their Hom bijections are precisely precomposition by $j^a$ or $j^0$, followed by the ordinary derived adjunction. It therefore identifies their units and counits and the completed pullback composition and identity maps defined as adjunction conjugates of direct-image composition and identity [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. The displayed reconstruction equality is natural in every morphism between complete inputs and under any isomorphism $r_VL\cong L_0$ of constant complete objects, with its induced strict reduction and completed-pullback maps. Direct image preserves completeness [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits], so the assertions apply also to $L=R_f^aK$ for complete $K$, with no properness, boundedness, constructibility or etale-origin condition.

source.place: Second paragraph: same reconstruction isomorphisms, strict coefficient supplement old Steps 9-11. Agent argument; Stacks 099M (proetale.tex, lemma-naive-completion), 099N (proetale.tex, lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case), with quotient-unit normalization as an additional comparison.

proof.text: Put $C_T^a=\mathcal L_T^a\mathcal R_T^a$ and $C_T^0=\mathcal L_T^0\mathcal R_T^0$, and denote their quotient units by $c^a,c^0$. Choose finite generators of $I$. Apply the ringed Koszul reflector to their images in $A_T$; the Koszul/quotient comparison identifies its unit with $c^a$. Thus $C_T^aM$ is complete and precomposition with $c_M^a$ is a bijection into every complete $A_T$-object, for every ambient $M$. The constant-coefficient completion adjunction gives the identical assertion for $C_T^0,c^0$. The coefficient equivalence identifies these local complete subcategories with those in the statement and says $A_T$ is flat over $\underline A_T$. Hence the exact restriction functors, their preservation of K-injectives, and the normalized scalar comparisons apply. No completeness of $M$ has been assumed.

source.place: Second paragraph, completion and reconstruction inputs; agent assembly of Stacks 099M and algebraization 099B/0A0E.

proof.text: Write $e_T^a:M\to\mathcal L_T^a\Delta M$ and $e_T^0:r_TM\to\mathcal L_T^0\Delta r_TM$ for the constant/limit maps used to construct the quotient units. The specified $\lambda$ satisfies $\lambda_{\Delta M}r_T(e_T^a)=e_T^0$. Indeed, choose a complex representing $M$ and a K-injective tower replacement $\Delta M\to H$. Restriction is exact and preserves K-injectives, so $\Delta r_TM\to r_TH$ is an allowed replacement for the other side. The first map is the compatible-family map $r_TM\to r_T\lim H$ followed by $r_T\lim H\to\lim r_TH$; the second is the map into $\lim r_TH$ with those same component maps. These are equal by the defining universal property of the ordinary limit. This computes the specified derived comparison, since its normalization is precisely the ordinary comparison conjugated by the total-derived units. The equality consequently holds on the derived categories, independently of the chosen replacement.

source.place: Second paragraph, normalization of the reconstruction maps: compatible-family calculation before applying quotient augmentation.

proof.text:
Let $h_M^a:\Delta M\to\mathcal R_T^aM$ and $h_{r_TM}^0:\Delta r_TM\to\mathcal R_T^0r_TM$ be the strict quotient augmentations. Define $\beta_M=\mathcal L_T^0(\rho_M)\lambda_{\mathcal R_T^aM}:r_TC_T^aM\xrightarrow{\sim}C_T^0r_TM$. Strict balancing says $\rho_Mr_T(h_M^a)=h_{r_TM}^0$. Naturality of $\lambda$ and Step 2 therefore give
$$\beta_Mr_T(c_M^a)=\mathcal L_T^0(\rho_Mr_T(h_M^a))\lambda_{\Delta M}r_T(e_T^a)=\mathcal L_T^0(h_{r_TM}^0)e_T^0=c_{r_TM}^0.$$
This proves the asserted identification of the actual completion units on every ambient input, using equality of strict augmentation maps before taking the limit.

source.place: Second paragraph, quotient-unit normalization of the same reconstruction isomorphisms.

proof.text:
Use the canonical pullback/tensor reassociation $\tau_{u,L}:\mathcal R_U^aL_u^aL\cong\mathscr L_u^a\mathcal R_V^aL$ from strict balancing. In the quotient-completion model for $F_u^a=C_U^aL_u^a$, its fixed reconstruction is $r_{u,L}=\mathcal L_U^a(\tau_{u,L})$; in any canonically identified model the same equation includes that model identification. The analogous constant reconstruction uses $\tau^0:\mathcal R_U^0G_u\cong G_u\mathcal R_V^0$. These identifications respect the maps from ordinary pullback: applying either side to its quotient augmentation sends a tensor $x$ to $x\otimes1$, at every quotient, with its quotient transition. They are exactly the strict-tower maps used in the definition of $j^a,j^0$, not maps selected from their evaluations. With the statement's convention suppressing $\tau^0$, naturality of $\lambda$ and the balancing equation give
$$\mathcal L_U^0(q_{u,L})\lambda_{\mathscr L_u^a\mathcal R_V^aL}r_U(r_{u,L})=r^0_{u,r_VL}\,C_U^0(a_{u,L})\beta_{L_u^aL}.$$
Indeed, move $\mathcal L_U^a(\tau_{u,L})$ across $\lambda$ by naturality and substitute $q_{u,L}r_U(\tau_{u,L})=\mathcal R_U^0(a_{u,L})\rho_{L_u^aL}$, with $\tau^0$ restored on the right when necessary.

source.place: Second paragraph, same reconstruction isomorphisms: explicit pullback/tensor and scalar normalization calculation.

proof.text:
Define $\phi_{u,L}=C_U^0(a_{u,L})\beta_{L_u^aL}$, using the quotient-completion models of Step 4. Both factors are natural isomorphisms, so this is a natural isomorphism; Step 4 is exactly its displayed reconstruction normalization in the statement. By Step 3 and naturality of $c^0$,
$$\phi_{u,L}r_U(j^a_{u,L})=C_U^0(a_{u,L})c^0_{r_UL_u^aL}=c^0_{G_ur_VL}a_{u,L}=j^0_{u,r_VL}a_{u,L}.$$
For uniqueness, $\beta_{L_u^aL}$ identifies $r_U(j^a_{u,L})$ with the constant completion unit. Since its target and $F_u^0r_VL$ are complete, precomposition with this unit is injective by the constant completion adjunction. Any other comparison satisfying the required equation equals $\phi_{u,L}$. This argument uses full faithfulness of restriction only on the complete subcategories; it makes no full-faithfulness assertion about the ambient categories.

source.place: Second paragraph, uniqueness of completion-unit normalized reconstruction comparison.

proof.text:
Let $L$ and $N$ be complete on $V$ and $U$, respectively. Direct image preserves completeness, so the ordinary adjunction restricts after composing with the completion reflector. Its Hom bijection sends $t:F_u^aL\to N$ first to $t j^a_{u,L}:L_u^aL\to N$, and then to its ordinary adjunct $L\to R_u^aN$. The first operation is bijective by Step 1; the second is the ordinary derived adjunction. This defines $F_u^a\dashv R_u^a$. On constant coefficients these are precisely the two Hom bijections specifying $F_u^0\dashv R_u^0$. To compare them put $t_0=r_U(t)\phi_{u,L}^{-1}$. The unit equation from Step 5 gives
$$t_0j^0_{u,r_VL}=r_U(tj^a_{u,L})a_{u,L}^{-1}.$$
The normalized scalar adjunction comparison says that the ordinary adjunct of the right side is $\chi_{u,N}r_V((tj^a_{u,L})^\sharp)$. Hence the two completed Hom bijections agree under restriction, $\phi$ and $\chi$. The coefficient equivalences on complete subcategories supply the required bijections on both Hom sets.

source.place: Second paragraph, completed adjunctions: explicit comparison of the two successive Hom bijections.

proof.text: A unit is the adjunct of the identity on the left-adjoint value, and a counit is the inverse adjunct of the identity on the right-adjoint value. Applying the equality of Hom bijections in Step 6 to these identities proves their compatibility, including the indicated $\phi$ and $\chi$ components. For composition, the scalar inverse-image comparisons $a_u$ come from the identical inverse image on underlying abelian sheaves, so the comparison for $uv$ equals the composite comparisons for $u$ and $v$, and the identity comparison is the identity. The ordinary direct-image composition maps are the adjunction conjugates of these inverse-image composition identifications. Applying the adjunct compatibility of flat restriction to their defining adjuncts shows that $\chi$ carries the completed-coefficient direct-image composition and identity maps to the constant-coefficient ones: both have the same adjunct, hence are equal. Finally the completed pullback composition and identity maps are, by definition, their conjugates for the completed adjunctions. Step 6 identifies those adjunctions, so applying the same Hom bijections to the defining conjugates identifies the completed pullback maps as well. Bijectivity of conjugation rules out any additional automorphism in these identifications.

source.place: Second paragraph, transport of units, counits and adjunction-conjugate composition/identity maps.

proof.text:
All maps used in Step 4 are natural transformations in the derived strict-tower categories: strict balancing supplies natural $\rho,q$, and the scalar limit square supplies natural $\lambda$. Thus applying functoriality to any morphism of complete inputs gives the reconstruction equality on that morphism. More explicitly, for an isomorphism $h:r_VL\xrightarrow{\sim}L_0$ of constant complete objects, postcompose the equality by $\mathcal L_U^0G_u(\mathcal R_V^0h)$. Naturality of $r^0$ gives
$$\mathcal L_U^0G_u(\mathcal R_V^0h)\mathcal L_U^0(q_{u,L})\lambda\,r_U(r_{u,L})=r^0_{u,L_0}F_u^0(h)\phi_{u,L}.$$
This is the asserted normalization after changing the identification of the constant complete input, with the induced strict reduction and completed-pullback maps. Invertibility of $h$ makes all comparison maps isomorphisms; the same computation works for arbitrary morphisms.

source.place: Second paragraph, naturality of the same reconstruction conjugations and change of complete input.

proof.text: For any morphism $f$ and any complete $K$, $R_f^aK$ is complete by direct-image preservation. Substitute $L=R_f^aK$ in Steps 4–8. Every argument there is in the unbounded ambient or full complete categories and uses only the stipulated coefficient datum. Consequently this substitution imposes none of properness, boundedness, constructibility, or etale origin.

source.place: Second paragraph, applicability to complete direct-image inputs.

proof_origin.place: Second paragraph: same reconstruction conjugations; explicit completion-unit and Hom-bijection normalization, using Stacks 099M/099N and 099B/0A0E.

split_report.summary: Split using existing nodes only. Compute preservation of the constant/limit map on a K-injective tower, then use the strict augmentation and pullback balancing equalities to identify quotient units and the fixed reconstruction maps. Derive uniqueness, completed Hom-bijection compatibility, units/counits and conjugate composition maps from the existing completion reflector and ordinary scalar adjunction comparison. No ambient full faithfulness or completeness of ordinary pullback is assumed.
